virus: Virus or viral surrogate studied. Includes human and animal viruses, bacteriophages, virus-like particles, and broader descriptors, with strain or serotype names when given
ph_before_treatment: pH measurement directly from source water sample or on site measurement
ph_after_treatment: Any pH adjustment done or that recorded after treatment
coagulant: Reported coagulant used in each study. Includes aluminum- and ferric-based salts (e.g., alum, ferric chloride/sulfate, polyaluminum chloride variants), proprietary formulations (e.g., PFC, PACl subtypes, Acquapol, Cat Floc, Primafloc), and less common coagulants (e.g., lime, chitosan, PEI). Entries reflect names exactly as given in the source
source_water: General category of the water matrix used in each study. Some examples include surface waters, raw or treated drinking water sources, wastewater (raw, secondary, filtered, or effluent), synthetic lab-prepared waters, spent filter backwash, and tap water
coagulant_dose: Reported numerical dose of primary coagulant prior to unit conversion. Store with unit of measurement
coagulant_aid_dose: Reported numerical dose of coagulant aid, typically in mg/L
temp: reported temperature in degrees Celsius when available
rapid_mix_time: Duration of the rapid mixing phase, typically reported in seconds or minutes. Value and unit of measurement is stored
rapid_mix_speed: Reported rapid mixing speed, measured in revolutions per minute (rpm)
flocculation_time: Duration of flocculation, typically recorded in minutes; may include multi-stage times if reported. Store value and unit of measurement
sedimentation_time: Reported settling duration following flocculation; measured in minutes
virus_measurement_methods: Technique used for virus quantification, recorded as reported. Method categories are qPCR, RT-qPCR, PCR, RT-PCR, real-time PCR, plaque assay, PFU, TCID₅₀ (including cell culture TCID₅₀/ml), enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA, e.g., NV-AD III kit), mouse assay, and radioimmunoassay (RIA endpoint titration)
spiked_concentration: Reported virus load added to samples, recorded in original study units (e.g., PFU/mL, TCID₅₀/mL, genome copies/mL, VLPs/mL). Values range from ~10² to >10¹¹ depending on assay and virus. Where studies provided log values or unusual formats (e.g., LD₅₀, PFU per 1000 L), these were transcribed directly
clay_addition: Type and concentration of clay added to synthetic waters (e.g., kaolin, bentonite, montmorillonite, clinoptilolite), reported in units such as mg/L, g/L, or ppm
sand_addition: Silica (SiO₂) additions, recorded as suspensions or concentrations in g/L or mg/L
alkalinity_addition: Added alkalinity sources (e.g., NaHCO₃ buffer, Ca(OH)₂, CaCO₃, sodium bicarbonate) with reported concentrations in mg/L, mM, or descriptive buffer volume
salt_addition: Added salts reported as ionic concentrations (e.g., Na⁺, Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺) or as CaCl₂ solutions across a range of molarities
organic_coagulant_aid: Type of organic polymeric aid used, recorded as reported (e.g., cationic, anionic, or nonionic polymers such as polyacrylamide, polyDADMAC, Cat Floc, Primafloc, Nalcolyte, Magnifloc)
inorganic_co-coagulant: Additional inorganic coagulants used alongside the primary coagulant (e.g., PASS-10, sodium aluminate), with reported doses when available
treatment_scale: Study implementation level: Bench = controlled lab trials (often jar tests); Pilot = reduced-scale systems replicating plant conditions; Full = operational treatment systems
rapid_mix_g: Intensity of rapid mixing, reported as velocity gradient (G-value) in s⁻¹
assay_details: Specific primers, kits, or methods used for virus detection, typically cited directly from prior studies or international standards (e.g., ISO10705-2). References and primer IDs are retained as reported.
flocculation_mixing_speed: Reported flocculation speeds, in rpm or G, sometimes subdivided into stages with varying intensities
number_of_samples: Reports replication and statistical treatment of experiments. Entries describe whether assays were run in duplicate, triplicate, or more (sometimes 3–6 runs), and may include details on plating replicates, averaging methods, or error bar representation. Some studies note single runs with duplicates for confirmation, or describe associated statistical analyses (e.g., ANOVA, variance tests).
alkalinity_initial: Initial alkalinity, most often measured directly from water samples, though in some cases set in lab conditions
alkalinity_final: Final alkalinity, typically measured from treated water samples, with some values from lab-controlled conditions
toc_percent_removal: Percent reduction in TOC reported in paper
uv254_initial: UV absorbance at 254 nm before treatment
uv254_final: UV absorbance at 254 nm after treatment
uv260_initial: UV absorbance at 260 nm before treatment
uv260_final: UV absorbance at 260 nm after treatment
virus_concentration: Measured virus concentration after treatment, as reported in the study
